symptoms: Severe headache, blurred vision, swelling of face and hands since morning
history: Primigravida, no prior ANC visits, no known medical history
justification: BP ≥160/110 mmHg with headache and visual disturbances meets criteria for severe preeclampsia. Immediate referral to FRU/CHC with IV MgSO4 and antihypertensives as per MOHFW maternal referral guidelines.

symptoms: Mild headache, mild pedal edema, no visual disturbances
history: G2P1, previous pregnancy normal, regular ANC
justification: BP 150/98 is elevated but below severe range; no severe features yet. Monitor closely, repeat BP in 4–6 hours, urine for protein, refer if BP worsens or proteinuria confirmed.

symptoms: Mild lower back pain, no bleeding, fetal movements normal
history: Primigravida, regular ANC, no complications
justification: All vitals normal, symptoms are common at term. Routine ANC counseling, birth preparedness plan, scheduled follow-up.

symptoms: Convulsion episode (tonic-clonic, ~2 min) witnessed by husband, now drowsy and confused
history: G3P2, no prior hypertension, no ANC in last 6 weeks
justification: Eclampsia — convulsion in a pregnant woman with high BP. Life-threatening emergency. Immediate referral with IV/IM MgSO4 loading dose, lateral positioning, IV antihypertensive en route.

symptoms: Heavy vaginal bleeding, soaked >5 pads in last 2 hours, feeling dizzy
history: G1P1, delivered vaginally at home, placenta delivered but bleeding persisted
justification: Primary/secondary PPH with haemodynamic compromise (low BP, dizziness). Immediate referral, IV access, uterotonic administration, IV fluids per AMTSL protocol.

symptoms: Burning urination, lower abdominal pain, chills, rigors since yesterday
history: G3P2, history of recurrent UTI in previous pregnancies
justification: Fever ≥38.5°C with rigors in pregnancy suggests pyelonephritis or sepsis. Risk of preterm labor. Immediate referral for IV antibiotics, blood and urine cultures, obstetric evaluation.

symptoms: Increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue
history: G2P1, family history of diabetes, previous baby weight >3.8 kg
justification: Fasting blood sugar 168 mg/dL with symptoms and risk factors is diagnostic of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Requires dietary counseling, glucose monitoring, endocrinology/specialist referral within 24–48 hours.

symptoms: Pallor, extreme fatigue, breathlessness on exertion, palpitations
history: Primigravida, vegetarian diet, no iron supplementation
justification: Clinical features suggest severe anaemia (likely Hb <7 g/dL). Breathlessness at rest is a danger sign. Immediate referral for Hb testing and possible blood transfusion as per MOHFW guidelines.

symptoms: Foul-smelling lochia, lower abdominal tenderness, malaise, chills
history: G2P2, delivered at home, placenta manually removed by TBA
justification: Postpartum endometritis/sepsis indicated by fever, foul lochia, and uterine tenderness after home delivery with instrumentation. Immediate referral for IV antibiotics and surgical evaluation.

symptoms: Mild swelling of feet in evenings, no headache, no vision changes
history: G2P1, no complications in last pregnancy, regular ANC
justification: Dependent pedal edema in mid-trimester without hypertension or proteinuria is physiological. Reassure, advise rest, elevation of legs, and routine follow-up.

symptoms: Headache, no visual disturbance, 1+ proteinuria on dipstick
history: Primigravida, BP was normal until 34 weeks
justification: BP 145/95 with proteinuria is mild preeclampsia at term. Monitor closely; if BP rises to ≥160/110 or symptoms worsen, immediate referral. Plan for delivery at FRU given term gestation.

symptoms: Severe nausea and vomiting, unable to retain fluids for 3 days, weight loss
history: Primigravida, first ANC visit today
justification: Hyperemesis gravidarum with dehydration risk. Unable to retain fluids for >24 hours warrants IV hydration and antiemetics. Refer to CHC if unable to maintain oral intake after initial management.

symptoms: Epigastric pain, nausea, headache, 2+ proteinuria on dipstick
history: G4P3, chronic hypertension, type 2 diabetes pre-pregnancy
justification: Severe preeclampsia with epigastric pain (possible HELLP syndrome) in a high-risk woman with comorbidities. Immediate referral for specialist care, MgSO4, antihypertensives, delivery planning.

symptoms: Breast engorgement, mild fever, breastfeeding difficulty, newborn latching poorly
history: G1P1, normal vaginal delivery at PHC
justification: Mild fever on day 2 is consistent with breast engorgement (milk let-down fever). Temperature <38°C. Support with breastfeeding counseling, warm compress, frequent feeding. Monitor for mastitis if fever persists.

symptoms: Severe headache since yesterday, visual blurring, no convulsions yet
history: G2P2, was normotensive throughout pregnancy, LSCS 5 days ago
justification: Postpartum preeclampsia with severe features (BP ≥160/110, headache, visual symptoms). Eclampsia can occur up to 6 weeks postpartum. Immediate referral with MgSO4 and antihypertensives.

symptoms: Mild spotting (brownish discharge), no pain, no heavy bleeding
history: Primigravida, previous period was regular, USG not done yet
justification: Threatened abortion — spotting in first trimester requires USG to rule out ectopic pregnancy and assess fetal viability. Refer for USG within 24 hours. Advise pelvic rest and watch for worsening bleeding.

symptoms: Sudden sharp lower right abdominal pain, dizziness, vaginal spotting, pain radiating to shoulder
history: G1P0, history of pelvic inflammatory disease, no USG done
justification: Ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise — unilateral pain, dizziness, referred shoulder pain (diaphragmatic irritation from hemoperitoneum), low BP. Life-threatening emergency; immediate surgical referral.

symptoms: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding, no contractions
history: G3P2, USG at 20 weeks showed low-lying placenta
justification: Painless antepartum hemorrhage with known low-lying placenta = placenta previa. Risk of massive hemorrhage. Do not perform vaginal exam. Immediate referral to hospital with blood bank and OT facilities.

symptoms: Sudden onset painful bleeding, hard tender uterus, decreased fetal movement
history: G2P1, alleged history of fall, hypertensive in this pregnancy
justification: Abruptio placentae — painful APH, board-like uterus, reduced fetal movements. Fetal and maternal life-threatening. Immediate emergency referral for emergency LSCS and resuscitation.

symptoms: Regular uterine contractions every 10 minutes, mild backache, no bleeding
history: Primigravida, previous preterm delivery in family history
justification: Preterm labor at 24 weeks (previable to periviable threshold). Requires tocolysis, antenatal corticosteroids, and immediate referral to facility with NICU capability.

symptoms: Reduced fetal movements since yesterday, no pain, no bleeding
history: G2P1, uncomplicated pregnancy, regular ANC
justification: Decreased fetal movements warrants urgent fetal surveillance (NST/CTG, fetal kick count assessment). Refer for fetal monitoring within a few hours. May indicate fetal compromise.

symptoms: Normal lochia, mild uterine cramping, breastfeeding initiated
history: G1P1, normal vaginal delivery at PHC, newborn healthy
justification: Normal postpartum status. Afterpains are physiological. Routine postnatal care, breastfeeding support, and 7-day follow-up recommended.

symptoms: High fever, breast redness and swelling, painful hard lump in left breast, chills
history: G2P2, exclusively breastfeeding, cracked nipples noted
justification: Mastitis with possible abscess formation. Temperature 39.1°C with localized breast signs. Requires antibiotics, analgesia, continued breastfeeding or pumping. Refer if abscess suspected (fluctuant mass) for surgical drainage.

symptoms: No complaints, routine visit, fetal movements started
history: Primigravida, regular ANC, Hb 10.2 g/dL at 12 weeks, on IFA tablets
justification: Asymptomatic, vitals normal, mild anaemia being managed with IFA. Routine ANC visit. Reinforce IFA compliance and nutritional counseling.

symptoms: Headache, blurred vision, 2+ proteinuria, fetal movements reduced
history: G4P3, known hypertensive on methyldopa, last delivery was LSCS
justification: Superimposed severe preeclampsia with worsening BP on antihypertensives, proteinuria, visual symptoms, and reduced fetal movements in a high-parity patient. Immediate referral with MgSO4 prophylaxis.

symptoms: Labor pains, regular contractions every 5 minutes, membranes intact, cervix 4 cm dilated
history: G2P1, previous normal delivery, no complications
justification: Active phase of labour, normal vitals. Well within normal progression. Manage at PHC/CHC with partograph monitoring. Refer only if complications develop.

symptoms: No labor pains, cervix unfavorable (Bishop score <4), mild pedal edema
history: Primigravida, regular ANC, no complications noted earlier
justification: Post-term pregnancy (41 weeks) with unfavorable cervix. Risk of placental insufficiency increases after 41 weeks. Refer for induction of labour to FRU/district hospital within 24 hours.

symptoms: Newborn (3 days old): fever 38.2°C, poor feeding, excessive crying, yellowish skin
history: Term delivery, birth weight 2.9 kg, no perinatal complications
justification: Neonatal fever (≥38°C in first week of life) combined with poor feeding suggests possible neonatal sepsis. Neonatal jaundice also needs assessment. Immediate referral to SNCU/NICU for evaluation and IV antibiotics.

symptoms: Newborn: birth weight 1.9 kg (preterm 34 weeks), unable to breastfeed, poor suck reflex
history: Preterm delivery by LSCS, admitted in SNCU for 2 days, now discharged
justification: Low birth weight preterm infant with poor feeding is at risk for hypoglycemia and sepsis. Kangaroo Mother Care, expressed breast milk by spoon/cup, close monitoring of temperature and feeding every 2–4 hours. Follow-up in 24 hours.

symptoms: Watery vaginal discharge since 2 days, no pain, no bleeding, no fever
history: G2P1, previous premature delivery at 30 weeks
justification: Prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM) suspected at 22 weeks in a patient with prior preterm birth. Risk of chorioamnionitis and cord prolapse. Immediate referral for speculum examination and obstetric care.

symptoms: Moderate lower back pain, urinary frequency, no dysuria, no fever
history: G1P0, Urine dipstick: no nitrites, no protein
justification: Musculoskeletal backache in third trimester without signs of UTI or preterm labour. Reassure, advise posture correction and back exercises, follow-up at next scheduled ANC.

symptoms: Extreme thirst, polyuria, recurrent episodes of vaginal candidiasis, fatigue
history: G3P2, family history of type 2 diabetes, two previous macrosomic babies
justification: Random blood sugar 210 mg/dL with symptoms in a high-risk patient with multiple GDM risk factors. Uncontrolled GDM. Urgent referral for OGTT confirmation, dietitian, and endocrinology consultation. Fetal monitoring required.

symptoms: Routine visit, mild fatigue, no complaints
history: Primigravida, Hb 9.0 g/dL at booking, on IFA tablets
justification: Hb 9.0 g/dL indicates moderate anaemia. Requires intensified IFA therapy, dietary counseling, and follow-up Hb at 20 weeks. Refer for IV iron infusion if Hb does not improve as per MOHFW guidelines.

symptoms: High fever, perineal wound (episiotomy site) red, swollen, purulent discharge
history: G1P1, vaginal delivery with episiotomy, delivery at home
justification: Perineal wound infection with systemic fever (38.8°C) in early postpartum. Risk of necrotizing fasciitis in perineal infections. Immediate referral for wound assessment, IV antibiotics, and possible surgical debridement.

symptoms: Feeling sad, tearful, not interested in baby, poor sleep, no thoughts of self-harm
history: G2P2, traumatic LSCS, husband working away, social isolation
justification: Probable postpartum depression (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale should be administered). Scores needing attention; no immediate danger but requires counseling, social support, and follow-up within 72 hours. Refer to ASHA/counselor.

symptoms: Breathlessness at rest, unable to lie flat, palpitations, cough
history: Primigravida, no cardiac history, but rheumatic fever in childhood
justification: Cardiac decompensation in pregnancy — breathlessness at rest and orthopnoea in a woman with childhood rheumatic fever (possible valvular disease). Immediate referral to tertiary care with cardiology and obstetrics.

symptoms: Mild nausea, heartburn, Braxton Hicks contractions, active fetal movements
history: G2P1, uncomplicated, last delivery normal
justification: Physiological complaints at term. Normal vitals and fetal movements. Reassure, antacids if needed, birth preparedness counseling, follow-up in 1 week.

symptoms: Wound redness at LSCS site, mild pain, no discharge, low-grade temperature
history: G1P1, emergency LSCS for fetal distress, PHC managed delivery
justification: Early wound infection signs at LSCS site. Temperature borderline. Monitor closely, wound dressing, oral antibiotics. Refer if fever increases, wound opens, or discharge appears.

symptoms: Mild edema feet, occasional headache, no visual complaints, no proteinuria on dipstick
history: G2P1, normal first pregnancy, family history of hypertension
justification: Borderline elevated BP (128/86) with mild edema and family history of hypertension. Gestational hypertension possible. Close BP monitoring, low-salt diet, repeat in 1 week. Refer if BP ≥140/90.

symptoms: Giddiness, fainting episode this morning, pallor, no bleeding
history: Primigravida, vegetarian, low income, Hb not checked yet
justification: Syncope in early pregnancy may indicate severe anaemia or hypotension. Requires urgent Hb testing and blood pressure assessment. If Hb <7, escalate to HIGH RISK for transfusion. Start IFA immediately.

symptoms: Reduced fetal movements past 24 hours, no headache, mild edema
history: G3P2, GDM diagnosed at 28 weeks, on dietary management only
justification: Uncontrolled GDM (fasting 178 mg/dL) combined with reduced fetal movements at 37 weeks strongly suggests fetal compromise. Immediate referral for NST/BPP and obstetric assessment. Risk of stillbirth.

symptoms: Newborn (day 1): not breastfeeding, weak cry, temperature 36.2°C (hypothermic), birth weight 2.1 kg
history: Term delivery but SGA baby, no perinatal asphyxia
justification: Neonatal hypothermia (temperature <36.5°C) in a low birth weight SGA newborn with poor feeding is a neonatal danger sign. Immediate warming (Kangaroo Mother Care), check blood glucose, refer to SNCU.

symptoms: No complaints, routine visit, large for dates uterus on palpation
history: G2P1, previous macrosomic baby 4.2 kg, no GDM screening done
justification: Uterus large for dates with history of macrosomic baby. GDM screening urgently required. Refer for OGTT, growth scan, and specialist review within 48 hours.

symptoms: Itching all over body, worse at night, palms and soles affected, no rash
history: Primigravida, no drug use, LFTs not done
justification: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) suspected — generalized pruritus without rash worsening at night, involving palms and soles. Risk of fetal distress/stillbirth. Refer for LFTs and bile acids within 24–48 hours.

symptoms: Heavy vaginal bleeding restarted (was normal till day 25), passing clots, mild cramps
history: G1P1, normal delivery, no retained placental issues noted
justification: Secondary PPH (bleeding after 24 hrs and up to 6 weeks postpartum). Could be due to retained products or endometritis. Refer for pelvic USG and gynecological evaluation within 24 hours. Monitor closely.

symptoms: Routine ANC, no complaints, fetal heart heard on Doppler
history: G1P0, Hb 11.5 g/dL, urine normal, on IFA and calcium
justification: Normal second trimester ANC visit. All parameters within acceptable range. Continue routine ANC, reinforce nutrition and IFA supplementation.

symptoms: Calf pain and swelling right leg, local warmth, difficulty walking
history: G2P2, elective LSCS, obese (BMI 32), immobilized for 3 days post-op
justification: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) suspected — calf pain, swelling, warmth in post-LSCS obese patient. Risk of pulmonary embolism (PE). Immediate referral for duplex USG and anticoagulation management.

symptoms: Extreme pallor of conjunctivae and palms, breathlessness even at rest, Hb 5.8 g/dL
history: Primigravida, tribal community, no IFA ever taken, poor diet
justification: Severe anaemia (Hb <7 g/dL) with breathlessness at rest is a maternal danger sign. Immediate referral for blood transfusion and IV iron therapy. Risk of high-output cardiac failure.

symptoms: Feeling anxious about labour, mild contractions, cervix 2 cm dilated, membranes intact
history: Primigravida, well-prepared for birth, no complications
justification: Latent phase of labour in a low-risk primigravida. Normal vitals. Manage expectantly at PHC with partograph monitoring. Encourage walking, hydration, support. Refer if active labour or complications develop.

symptoms: Swelling of face, headache, 1+ proteinuria, no visual symptoms
history: Primigravida adolescent, married recently, no prior ANC
justification: Early preeclampsia in adolescent primigravida (BP 142/92 with proteinuria). High-risk age group. Needs close monitoring, antihypertensives if BP worsens, and referral to FRU. Daily BP monitoring, rest, low-salt diet.

symptoms: No complaints, passing normal lochia, breastfeeding well, baby alert and active
history: G2P2, normal vaginal delivery, no perinatal complications
justification: Normal postpartum recovery. Breastfeeding established. Routine postnatal care, family planning counseling, iron-folate continuation, 7-day follow-up.

symptoms: Mild fatigue, no other complaints, GDM screening done today
history: G3P2, BMI 29, previous GDM in last pregnancy
justification: Post-prandial blood sugar 155 mg/dL with history of prior GDM. GDM management needed — dietary modification, glucose monitoring, and specialist follow-up within 1 week for treatment plan.

symptoms: Fever, uterine contractions, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, fetal tachycardia on auscultation (FHR 175/min)
history: G1P0, membranes ruptured 18 hours ago at home
justification: Chorioamnionitis — fever, foul amniotic fluid, and fetal tachycardia after prolonged PROM. Life-threatening to mother and fetus. Immediate referral for IV antibiotics and expedited delivery.

symptoms: Mother: recovering well. Newborn: deep jaundice (scleral icterus, jaundice extending to palms and soles), not feeding well
history: Term baby, birth weight 3.1 kg, blood group O+ mother, baby A+
justification: Pathological neonatal jaundice with feeding difficulty, extending to palms and soles by day 3, suggests significant hyperbilirubinemia possibly due to ABO incompatibility. Risk of kernicterus. Immediate referral for serum bilirubin and phototherapy/exchange transfusion.

symptoms: Cord felt outside vagina after membranes ruptured spontaneously, baby not yet delivered
history: G1P0, fetal presentation was transverse on last visit
justification: Cord prolapse — obstetric emergency with immediate risk of fetal death from cord compression. Immediate referral, knee-chest position, elevate presenting part, IV access, emergency LSCS needed.

symptoms: Mild leg cramps at night, some ankle swelling, sleeping poorly
history: G1P0, no prior complaints, calcium supplements prescribed
justification: Night leg cramps and mild ankle edema are common physiological complaints in third trimester. Normal vitals. Reassure, ensure calcium supplementation, advise stretching exercises.

symptoms: No vaginal bleeding, lochia subsiding, breastfeeding well, recovering from LSCS
history: G2P2, elective LSCS for breech, uneventful recovery
justification: Normal postpartum recovery at 2 weeks post-LSCS. Wound healing, lochia settling, breastfeeding established. Routine postnatal follow-up at 6 weeks.

symptoms: Regular contractions, membranes ruptured 4 hours ago, meconium-stained amniotic fluid (thick green), FHR 160/min
history: G1P0, gestational hypertension diagnosed at 36 weeks
justification: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid with possible fetal tachycardia indicates fetal distress. High-risk delivery requiring skilled birth attendant, paediatrician at delivery, and NICU standby. Immediate transfer to FRU.

symptoms: Routine visit, no complaints, uterine size appropriate, fetal movements good
history: G1P0, Hb 11.8 g/dL, urine normal
justification: Normal third trimester ANC. All parameters satisfactory. Schedule next visit at 32 weeks, continue IFA and calcium supplementation, TT booster if not given.

symptoms: Uterus not contracted (atonic), continued heavy bleeding after delivery of placenta, pallor, weak pulse
history: G4P4, prolonged labour, delivered at home
justification: Primary PPH due to uterine atony — high parity, atonic uterus, haemodynamic compromise. Immediate life-saving measures: bimanual uterine compression, oxytocin/misoprostol, IV fluids, immediate transfer.

symptoms: New-onset headache, mild swelling of face, trace proteinuria on dipstick, no visual symptoms
history: G2P1, previous preeclampsia, on aspirin 75 mg from 16 weeks
justification: Recurrent preeclampsia suspected in a known high-risk patient. BP 148/96 not yet in severe range. Requires close BP monitoring, BP diary, urine protein repeat, and daily review. Refer to FRU for decision on timing of delivery.

symptoms: No symptoms, referred by ASHA for ANC registration
history: Primigravida, first visit to PHC, Hb 12.2 g/dL, no risk factors
justification: Late but normal ANC registration. No high-risk features. Register in JSY scheme, initiate IFA and calcium, schedule next visit in 4 weeks, educate on danger signs.

symptoms: Regular contractions since 6 hours, 8 cm cervical dilation, membranes bulging, FHR normal
history: G2P1, previous normal delivery, no complications
justification: Advanced active labour in a multiparous woman with uncomplicated history. Normal FHR and vitals. Manage delivery at PHC with skilled birth attendant, partograph monitoring, prepare for imminent delivery.

symptoms: Routine 6-week postpartum visit, breastfeeding well, mild fatigue, some hair loss
history: G2P2, normal recovery post-LSCS, no complications
justification: Normal 6-week postnatal visit. Hair loss and fatigue are common postpartum. Check Hb, counsel on family planning, continue iron supplementation if Hb low.

symptoms: High fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion
history: G1P1, home delivery, no complications noted at delivery
justification: Meningitis suspected — fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, and altered consciousness in postpartum period. May also indicate postpartum sepsis extending to CNS. Immediate referral to tertiary care with IV antibiotics.

symptoms: Decreased fetal movement today, abdominal tightening, no bleeding
history: G1P0, normal ANC, recent history of diarrhea and dehydration 3 days ago
justification: Reduced fetal movements following recent dehydration episode. Risk of fetal compromise. Requires fetal kick count monitoring, hydration, and CTG/NST if available. Refer if movements do not improve within 2–4 hours.

symptoms: Mild constipation, haemorrhoids, rectal bleeding (small amount), no abdominal pain
history: G2P1, history of haemorrhoids in last pregnancy
justification: Haemorrhoidal bleed in pregnancy without anaemia or other complications. Reassure, high-fiber diet, increase fluids, safe topical agents, and routine follow-up.

symptoms: Newborn: umbilical cord red, swollen with pus discharge, baby irritable, temperature 37.9°C
history: Home delivery, cord cut with unsterile blade, no cord care done
justification: Omphalitis with pus and periumbilical redness after unsterile cord cutting. Risk of neonatal sepsis and tetanus. Immediate referral for IV antibiotics, neonatal assessment, and tetanus immunoglobulin evaluation.

symptoms: Large uterus for dates, twin pregnancy confirmed on earlier USG, no contractions
history: G2P1, twin pregnancy diagnosed at 20 weeks, no other complications
justification: Twin pregnancy at 37 weeks requires delivery planning at a facility with NICU capability. Borderline fasting sugar needs GDM management. Refer to FRU for delivery planning and monitoring.

symptoms: High fever, productive cough with yellow sputum, breathlessness, Sp02 not measurable at this facility
history: G1P1, had home delivery, was in contact with TB patient
justification: Postpartum pneumonia or possible TB reactivation. Fever, productive cough, and breathlessness in postpartum period. Immediate referral for CXR, sputum AFB, blood cultures, O2 support.

symptoms: Mild perineal discomfort (episiotomy), normal lochia, breastfeeding 6–8 times per day, urinating normally
history: G1P1, vaginal delivery at CHC with episiotomy, no perineal infection signs
justification: Normal postpartum recovery with expected perineal discomfort. Episiotomy healing normally. Provide analgesia, sitz baths, hygiene education, and scheduled 7-day postnatal visit.

symptoms: Moderate headache, blurred vision starting 2 hours ago, 2+ proteinuria, contracting mildly
history: G4P3, on no antihypertensives, no ANC for 6 weeks
justification: Preeclampsia with severe features approaching eclampsia threshold — visual symptoms, 2+ proteinuria, in a high-parity patient in labour without care. Immediate referral with MgSO4 and antihypertensive therapy.

symptoms: Mild breathlessness on exertion, Hb 8.2 g/dL (done today), pallor, no pedal edema
history: G2P1, moderate anemia, poor compliance with IFA
justification: Moderate anaemia (Hb 8–10.9 g/dL) at 34 weeks. No breathlessness at rest. Intensify IFA therapy, consider IV iron infusion, dietitian referral. Follow-up Hb in 4 weeks; refer if Hb <8 or deteriorates.

symptoms: Newborn (day 2): mild yellowish tinge of skin (face only), feeding well, active, temperature 37.0°C, birth weight 3.0 kg
history: Term delivery, no perinatal complications, mother O+, baby B+
justification: Physiological neonatal jaundice — mild, limited to face, day 2, term baby, feeding well. Encourage breastfeeding frequently (8–12 times/day), monitor for extension to chest/abdomen. Review in 24 hours.

symptoms: High fever, rigors, uterine tenderness, offensive lochia, tachycardia (pulse 118/min), appears toxic
history: G3P3, home delivery by TBA, retained membrane suspected, no antibiotics given
justification: Postpartum sepsis with systemic inflammatory response — high fever, tachycardia, uterine tenderness, offensive lochia after suspected retained products. MOHFW maternal danger sign. Immediate referral for IV antibiotics, uterine evaluation, and ICU-level care if needed.
